findings.text: a source update that empties a signal's feed description reaches the writer with embed_text '' while the signal carries a generated description, so the empty_text arm writes the empty text's hash and sets embedding and embedded_at to null, destroying the vector for a text that is now the indexed generated description; the lambda at line 291 returns item['description'] for a generated row, which is empty in exactly this case, and the vector should be left alone as it is when the description is non-empty.

the suite bullet states the changed tree fails one prompt-schema walk and the base tree's only other failure is a 30-second timeout, which describes the earlier default-tier arms; the arms recorded in the manifest's baseline_suite and after_suite at 0aa4b347 and 3e290e15 report 34 and 31 failures over -m 'not slow' with the failing ids being live-graph data and standard-name state on both sides, so the evidence narrative does not reconcile with the logs it points a reader to even though the measured conclusion (no added failure) holds.

the record's commits list names three shas and omits 3e290e15, the commit the after_suite arm actually ran at, and changed_paths omits tests/discovery/test_signal_glossary.py and tests/discovery/test_signals_pipeline.py, both carried by that commit; failure_attribution at line 20 likewise describes the earlier arms at base and c92bd864 (28 failures, one head-only catalogue-text test that now passes), so three manifest fields disagree with the arms they cite.
